rounds.text: Retaggio Industries Ltd is profoundly under-appreciated by the market, trading at an exceptionally modest P/E multiple of 10.5x and a price-to-book ratio of just 1.38x against a book value of ₹ 34.5 [E1, E2]. This low valuation stands in stark contrast to the company's stellar fundamental performance, highlighted by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 54% and a phenomenal trailing twelve months sales growth of 258% [E8, E9]. Profitability metrics are equally compelling, with a 3-year compounded profit growth of 43% and a staggering trailing twelve months profit growth of 268% [E10, E11]. Furthermore, the business generates elite returns, boasting a ROCE of 20.8%, an ROE of 21.4%, and a 5-year median ROE of 21% [E6, E7, E13]. Valuation models underscore this disconnect, as a discounted cash flow analysis indicates an intrinsic value of ₹ 184 per share, leaving a massive margin of safety of 74.2%, while a reverse DCF reveals that today’s price absurdly implies negative earnings growth [E29, E30, E31]. Conceded: operating cash flow is negative at Rs -25.24 Cr in Mar 2026, cash conversion stands at -2.82x, and promoter holding dropped from 99.99% to 55.06% [E19, E20, E26].

Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 10.5x and a price-to-book ratio of 1.38x [E1, E2], and boasts a 3-year compounded sales growth of 54% alongside a 3-year compounded profit growth of 43% [E8, E10]. Conceded: ROCE stands at 20.8% and ROE is 21.4% [E6, E7], while a discounted cash flow calculates an intrinsic value of ₹ 184 against a market price of ₹ 47.5 [E29]. However, this reported fundamental strength is completely undermined by a severe liquidity crisis, evidenced by operating cash flow collapsing to negative ₹ 25.24 Cr and free cash flow sinking to negative ₹ 25.30 Cr in Mar 2026 [E20, E21]. Conceded: a reverse DCF implies negative earnings growth [E31], but that matches the reality that cash conversion has plunged to -2.82x [E19] and borrowings have jumped to ₹ 18.96 Cr [E24]. Furthermore, the bull ignores massive insider exodus, with promoter holding crashing by 44.93 percentage points down to 55.06% [E26], while operational efficiency deteriorates through high debtors of 215 days [E37] and a falling operating margin of 14% [E16].
